tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)

The metric used for the Medical Image Deidentification Benchmark (MIDI-B) challenge will be deviation
from the answer key.
b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

The MIDI-B challenge is a rule-based de-identification challenge. The metric for success lies in an
algorithm's ability to accurately anonymize PHI/PII in images, conform to the DICOM standard, and
perform best practices, as described in the challenge instructions.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Ranking will be based on anonymization of DICOM metadata and burnt-in information in three categories:
HIPAA identifiers, DICOM Standard, and Best practice. A link to the HIPAA identifiers is provided in the
Reference section.
b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.
A missing result will count as a zero entry, or failed attempt at deidentification of the subject image.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

 Medical Image De-Identification Benchmark

Deidentification of PHI/PII is required by law to preserve patient privacy. We will provide each participant
with the result of their algorithm performance in each of the three categories.

Run reproducible analyses on shared data with documented provenance. Coordinate consortium science across disease areas including Alzheimer's disease, neurofibromatosis, ALS, rare cancers, and others.
